analysis.title: Year Ahead 2027: Commodity Outlook
key_insights: BofA is bullish industrial metals and grains and neutral on oil, precious metals and softs for 2027. MLCX and BCOM total return indices are up 64% and 21% ytd, led by energy on the US-Iran war and Russia-Ukraine infrastructure damage.

Brent is forecast to average $80/bbl and WTI $70/bbl in 2027, with a return to a ~1.5mn b/d surplus. Outcomes are binary: scenario averages are $70 (peace deal), $100 (fragile status quo) and $130 (kinetic escalation, with front-month spikes above $150).

Oil supply disruptions hit a record, with ~18mn b/d offline at peak. Global stocks peaked at 6.0bn bbl in March and are being drawn fast, with OECD SPRs and Chinese commercial stocks depleted. Brent front-to-third spread peaked at $21/bbl while long-dated prices barely moved, so the curve discounts normalization.

Refined products are tighter than crude. ICE gasoil cracks are near $80/bbl and NYH distillate cracks are above $100/bbl, with Russian refining 51% affected and low global utilization. BofA is overweight RBOB and gasoil, and sees 2027 ULSD-Brent cracks averaging $43/bbl (Exhibit 3).

Copper is forecast to flip to a 142kt deficit in 2027, with LME cash averaging $14,625/t and a 4Q27 forecast of $16,000. US warehouse financing deals hold 1.7mt of refined copper and keep the market tight, and a Chinese grid-spending rebound is the key 2H27 upside driver.

Aluminium should reach $3,500/t in 1H27 on pent-up US and Europe demand and low LME stocks. A small 431kt surplus builds in 2H27 as Indonesian supply rises, and the 2027 average is $3,188/t. Zinc moves to a 114kt deficit and nickel to a 213kt deficit, contingent on Indonesia's 2027 RKAB permits.

AI is the key demand pillar: hyperscaler capex is above $800bn in 2026 and about $1.2tn in 2027. Asian chip exports correlate with copper and oil returns, with copper more sensitive. Democratic midterm wins and state data center ballot measures raise friction risk, but BofA expects the impact mostly from 2028.

Gold is forecast at $3,750 in 1Q27 rising to $5,000 by 4Q27, with the 2027 average at $4,438. Headwinds are a stronger USD, higher real yields, oil and a Fed hiking cycle, plus weak ETF buying and Indian demand. BofA expects a muted start to 2027 and a rally in 2H.

Silver is forecast to go from an 11kt deficit in 2025 to a small surplus, with a $75/oz intra-year high possible in 2027. Gold is its closest correlate, and data centers will not save or sink the market.

Grains: wheat could reach $7-8/bu if Black Sea disruptions persist versus $5.50 on de-escalation. Black Sea wheat exports are down ~15mn t (40%) yoy in July-December. Corn is expected to recover to $5/bu by spring, with a $4.50 floor on Brazil safrinha and de-escalation. EU grain output falls 10% and EU corn imports hit a record 26-27mn t.

Soybeans average $11.80/bu in 2027E, with a $11 downside if US output beats USDA or China imports weaken. Soybean oil averages 63c/lb, and BofA is more confident in crush demand than in Chinese import demand. Sugar is bullish at 18-19c/lb on EU, India and CS Brazil production losses tied to El Niño.

US natural gas stays muted: Henry Hub is forecast at $3.35/MMBtu for 2027, with a super El Niño and loose balances as downside risks and winter deliverability as the only upside risk. TTF could spike above €120/MWh in a cold winter but averages €55/MWh. BofA is underweight natural gas.

Macro backdrop: the Fed has returned to hikes, with OIS pricing more hikes, and global growth is forecast at 3.4% in 2026 and 2027. US energy share of disposable income is 3.4%, so consumption is resilient. Yields are up as much as 130bps in France and 90bps in the US ytd.

Portfolio strategy: roll returns were nearly half of 2026 commodity returns. The expected carry across 6-12 month rolls is negative in aggregate, so 2027 returns lean on oil. A 40-40-20 portfolio beat 60-40 in 9 of 12 high-inflation periods, and rolling more often captures backwardation.

sector_views.rationale: AI and grid demand, low stocks, tight mine supply and financing-deal inventory lock-up support copper, aluminium and zinc.
Black Sea disruption, EU crop losses, low Chinese stocks and El Niño risk support wheat and corn.
Brent baseline is $80 but outcomes are binary on the wars, with peace pointing to $70 and escalation to $130.
Refinery damage, Russian export loss and low utilization keep diesel and gasoline cracks elevated.
Loose US storage balances and El Niño risk cap prices outside winter cold events.
Rates and USD headwinds persist into early 2027, with gold seen rallying in 2H and silver finding a base.
Sugar is overweight on supply losses, while coffee, cotton and cocoa are neutral.
Neutral price view with a negative roll yield view for lean hogs.

risk_factors: A durable peace deal could compress energy and grain risk premia, with Brent near $70.
A cut to AI and data center capex would hit industrial metals.
Renewed US-Iran war could push Brent to $130 average and above $150 at times.
Tighter monetary policy with Fed hikes, a stronger USD and higher real yields weigh on gold and silver.
A US refined copper tariff decision could cause volatility in time spreads.
Indonesian supply growth in aluminium and nickel permit decisions.
Mild winter from a super El Niño could pressure natural gas.
Depleted OECD and Chinese oil stocks leave little buffer against another supply shock.
Data center restrictions after the Democratic midterm sweep, mostly from 2028.
charts_described: Exhibit 5 shows ytd MLCX sector returns of energy +111%, industrial metals +64%, with precious metals at -16% and grains/softs near +2-3%.
Exhibit 218-type backtests aside, Exhibit 24 and 25 text states hyperscaler capex above $800bn in 2026 and around $1.2tn in 2027.
Exhibit 28 text says global oil supply disruptions have never been as high as in 2026, at ~18mn b/d at peak.
Exhibit 144 table shows ETF purchases -45.4% yoy, central banks +79.7% yoy, China imports +39.3% yoy and India imports -77.8% yoy.
vol_and_positioning: Commodity roll returns made up nearly half of 2026 index returns, and the aggregate 1-year backwardation z-score is close to one standard deviation above its historical average.
Brent front-to-third-month spread peaked at $21/bbl and Dated Brent traded at a steep premium to the front month.
Managed money corn longs were unwound as corn fell from $5.45 to $4.40/bu.
Gold ETF AUM has risen even as gold fell, which BofA calls trapped length that could pressure prices if investors sell.
Rolling 1-year correlation of BCOM with equities and bonds is at its lowest in 25 years.
Rolling more frequently to monetize backwardation and shortening tenor is recommended in backwardated bull markets.
geopolitical: US-Iran war is now nine months old, with weekly attacks on vessels near the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf crude exports recovering to ~7.4mn b/d in September.
Russia-Ukraine: Ukrainian drone strikes affect 51% of Russian refining capacity and Russia has restricted exports, while attacks constrain Black Sea grain flows.
Saudi-Houthi conflict and rerouting of ~4mn b/d via the East-West pipeline to the Red Sea raised Suez crossings.
Democrats won the House, Senate and key governorships in the midterms. BofA sees this as lowering odds of Iran escalation and raising friction for data center build-out.
US-China trade: a $17bn ag purchase deal with China more than $5bn behind its pro-rated 2026 commitment, and uncertainty over a US refined copper tariff.
Indonesia is curbing nickel mining permits (RKAB) and has a moratorium on new smelters.
Prediction markets (Kalshi) see no near-term resolution of the US-Iran conflict but greater odds of a solution over 12-24 months.

tension_points.bull_case: Continued or renewed US-Iran war keeps Brent near $100 or $130 average with spikes above $150.
tension_points.bear_case: A peace deal restores flows and inventory rebuilding, pulling Brent below $70 and WTI below $60 at times, and long-dated prices already discount normalization.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A signed US-Iran peace deal, or sustained Hormuz transit recovery with refinery restarts, would invalidate the upside case.

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscaler capex rises to ~$1.2tn in 2027, adding ~$400bn, supporting copper and aluminium.
tension_points.bear_case: Democratic midterm wins and data center ballot limits could slow build-out, and a capex downward revision would hit industrial metals.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A meaningful downward revision in capex would invalidate the bullish industrial metals thesis.

tension_points.bull_case: Fiscal deficits, US gridlock and uncertainty push gold to $5,000 by 4Q27.
tension_points.bear_case: Fed hikes, stronger USD, higher real yields and weak ETF and Indian buying keep early 2027 muted, and ETF length could unwind.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Continued Fed tightening and USD strength with rising oil would delay the rally, per the report's own conditions.
